impacts.summary: Everything this printing plant reports goes into the air as ozone, about 46,600 lb in 2024.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: Ground-level ozone irritates the airways, causing coughing, a sore throat and chest tightness. Packaging printers usually make it with equipment that treats plastic film before printing. Ozone breaks down within hours, so the effect stays close to the plant.

impacts.summary: Almost all of this mill's releases go straight into the Fox River, about 2 miles above where it meets the bay.

impacts.title: Fish & river life
impacts.how: About 230,000 lb of nitrates and 150 lb of ammonia reached the river in 2024. Extra nutrients feed algae that use up the oxygen fish need to breathe, and ammonia is directly toxic to fish at high levels. The mill also released 57 lb of lead, which settles into river mud and builds up in fish over time.

avoid.text: Use less lawn fertilizer: runoff adds even more nutrients to the same river

impacts.title: Swimming & beaches
impacts.how: The Fox River carries these nutrients into the bay, where they can help fuel algae blooms that close beaches and turn the water green. The Fox is already listed as impaired for nutrients; this mill is one possible contributor.

impacts.summary: Manitowoc's city-owned power plant released about 9,200 lb to the air in 2024, mostly hydrochloric acid from burning fuel.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: About 7,200 lb of hydrochloric acid and 2,000 lb of ammonia went into the air. Both irritate the eyes, nose and lungs. Sources disagree on its fuel: federal energy data lists mostly wood and wood waste, but the utility said in 2025 that its two main boilers still burn mostly coal and petroleum coke. It is converting them to pellets made from paper and plastic waste.

impacts.how: EPA added 1-bromopropane to its list of hazardous air pollutants in 2022, and TRI flags it as a carcinogen. Long-term exposure can also harm the nervous system.
